newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranian rial slides on demand for hard cash.
newsitem.headline: Iranian rial slides on demand for hard cash.

text.p: The Iranian rial has fallen by six percent against the dollar in the past few weeks on strong demand for hard currencies, money dealers said on Friday.
London-based Iranian trader Ali Pakpour said his firm was selling dollars at up to 4,930 rials each in Europe, compared to 4,640 in mid-October.
The German mark sold for 3,210 rials, the pound sterling 8,270 rials and the French franc 940 rials, he said.
In Dubai, a major trading post for Iranian private business and state firms, one dollar cost 4,930 rials at the end of the business week on Thursday, one trader said.
"There is high demand for dollars from Iranian exporters who want to fulfil their state obligations early," Pakpour said.
Iran's foreign exchange regulations require exporters to return their hard cash income home and exchange it at state banks at the official rate of 3,000 rials to the dollar.
Pakpour said authorities were giving various bonuses to encourage exporters to repatriate their hard currencies early.
The rial lost about five percent of its value against the dollar during September and early October.
The rial's slide had pushed up speculative demand for dollars on a reactivated black market, Tehran residents said.
One resident said each dollar was being sold for about 4,800 rials on Thursday on the Tehran black market.
